items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Terminology 3:1
items.html: ZA and the Nukva of Atzilut are regarded as the discernment of one in partnership. For although the Nukva is entirely Gevurot, still the whole of ZA’s wholeness depends upon his union with her, and the light of Ein Sof does not indicate ZA except at the time of his union with the Nukva. Thus they are one in partnership, for the light of His unity dwells only in their partnership together. This is not so with AA, who has no discernment of a separated Nukva — (A note: our master the author explained in the Idra Rabba that his left returns to the right, in the secret of “white within white.”) — that is, one that would be entirely Gevurot and separated from him. Therefore the male and the female are counted as a single Partzuf. This is the secret of the verse, “and there is no god with Me,” meaning that he has no partnership with a Nukva. (p. 648, Item 52)
